entries.clue: Who might be streaming abroad? (9)

indicatorNotes.abroad: abroad also means astray or all over the place, so the letters scatter

annotation.surface: A question about which people might be pouring out of their country.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: read straight, it describes people flowing overseas; read as instructions, it sends STREAMING abroad into a new order.
annotation.definitionFit: Emigrants leave their homeland to settle overseas, often in large flows the news calls streams.

entries.clue: Revolutionary work introduced by English writer (5)

indicatorNotes.Revolutionary: a revolution turns something right round, so the word is read backwards
indicatorNotes.introduced by: the following piece is preceded by the first one

annotation.surface: A radical piece of writing launched by an English author.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read in answer order: English comes first because it introduces the reversed work.
annotation.definitionFit: George Eliot and T. S. Eliot are both famous writers.

entries.clue: Boringly spin around, lazily following current (9)

indicatorNotes.following: IDLY comes after the letter for current

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: Someone lazily drifting and turning in a current, rather dully.
annotation.walkthrough: The river picture hides that current is the physics symbol I, which sits first; the shuffled SPIN and IDLY follow it.
annotation.definitionFit: Something done insipidly is done in a dull, flavourless, boring way.

entries.clue: Dog otter struggling with large weir (10)

indicatorNotes.struggling: letters that struggle are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing sizes

annotation.surface: A dog otter battling against a big weir on a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dog otter' reads as one phrase, a male otter; the definition is just 'Dog', and 'otter' starts the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: The Rottweiler is a large German breed of dog.

entries.clue: In poor health bearing note: it's catching (7)

indicatorNotes.bearing: in a down answer, AILING carries N on top of it

annotation.surface: A sick person warns that what they have is contagious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It's catching' reads as a warning about infection, which fits the poor health; it is really the definition, as in nailing a culprit.
annotation.definitionFit: Nailing someone is catching or pinning them down, as police nail a suspect.

entries.clue: Fancy South American reportedly grabbed quick kiss (7)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is heard, so we want a word's sound

annotation.surface: An attractive South American is said to have snatched a quick kiss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective or a crush; it is the verb, as in 'I fancy he's lying'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of a hunch: 'I fancy he's lying' and 'I suspect he's lying' say the same.

entries.clue: Bogged down setter about to punch boss (5)

indicatorNotes.to punch: a punch goes into something, so I and RE go inside MD

blocks.note: the setter refers to themselves as I

annotation.surface: A frustrated setter, stuck in a rut, lashes out at the boss.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter's I and RE go inside the managing director.
annotation.definitionFit: Mired means stuck in mud, and figuratively bogged down.

entries.clue: Youth, perhaps, spy ring replaced with adult (4)

indicatorNotes.replaced with: one letter is swapped out for another

blocks.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

annotation.surface: A young person who might be a spy, in a ring swapped for a grown-up.
annotation.walkthrough: O looks like a ring, and A is the old film certificate for adult.
annotation.definitionFit: A youth is a young man, so an example of a male; 'perhaps' marks the example.

entries.clue: One playing with sticks and hoops (5)

blocks.note: the letter O is shaped like another hoop

annotation.surface: A child playing a garden game with sticks and hoops.
annotation.walkthrough: The sticks are drumsticks: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer.
annotation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr played drums, with sticks, for the Beatles.

entries.clue: Fighters expected pound to enter field of combat (9)

indicatorNotes.to enter: to enter is to go in, so the pound sign L goes into the jousting ground LISTS

blocks.note: the lists were the enclosed ground for jousting

annotation.surface: Warriors who were anticipated are ready to pound onto the battlefield.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pound' reads as a verb of attack; it is the money sign L, slipped in just after the first L of LISTS.
annotation.definitionFit: Duellists are fighters who meet in a duel.

entries.clue: Some poinsettias displayed in a corner (5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes an inset, such as a small map set in the corner of a larger one

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters are used

blocks.note: letters three to seven of the plant's name

annotation.surface: A few Christmas poinsettias are put on show in the corner of a room.
annotation.walkthrough: The Christmas picture makes 'displayed in a corner' read as flower arranging; it describes a small picture set into a larger one.
annotation.definitionFit: An inset is a small picture or map set within a larger one, usually in a corner.

entries.clue: Hotel chef periodically checking fish sauce (9)

indicatorNotes.checking: to check something is to hold it in, so INN holds SOLE

blocks.note: C h E f: every other letter

annotation.surface: A hotel chef keeps checking on the sauce for the fish.
annotation.walkthrough: In a kitchen scene 'sauce' reads literally; it is the British sense of cheek or impudence.
annotation.definitionFit: Sauce, in British usage, is cheeky impudence, which is insolence.

entries.clue: Collection of keys I sort in the van (10)

indicatorNotes.in the van: the van is the vanguard, the front, so TYPE goes ahead of WRITER

blocks.note: a sort is a type or kind
I is the setter, the writer of this puzzle

annotation.surface: Someone sorting a bunch of keys while sitting in a van.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface van is a vehicle; here it is short for vanguard, the front. 'I' in a clue often means the setter, so the writer.
annotation.definitionFit: By description: a typewriter is essentially a bank of keys that strike letters onto paper.

entries.clue: Kitty's eye looking the wrong way (4)

indicatorNotes.looking the wrong way: facing backwards, the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: the eye of a hook and eye is a small loop

annotation.surface: A cat with a squint, one eye pointing off in the wrong direction.
annotation.walkthrough: Kitty looks like a cat; it is a shared fund of money. The 's stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pool of money that several people contribute to.

entries.clue: Lack of activity unsettling antagonist (10)

indicatorNotes.unsettling: the letters are unsettled, disturbed out of order

annotation.surface: A period of inaction is disturbing an opponent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unsettling' reads as an adjective describing the antagonist; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stagnant water does not move, and an economy in stagnation is idle.

entries.clue: Bear, having lost weight, treading softly (7)

indicatorNotes.having lost: what a word has lost it no longer holds, so TON drops off PADDINGTON

blocks.note: Paddington, the bear from the children's books
a ton is a weight; it comes off the end

annotation.surface: A bear who has slimmed down now moves quietly.
annotation.walkthrough: Paddington is the fictional bear from Peru named after a London railway station.
annotation.definitionFit: Padding is walking with soft, quiet steps.

entries.clue: Assume position with university behind schedule (9)

blocks.note: a post is a position or job

annotation.surface: Someone takes up a university job that is running late.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces run in the order the clue gives them.
annotation.definitionFit: To postulate is to assume something as a basis for reasoning.

entries.clue: One counting, presumably, on first of Scottish reels (7)

indicatorNotes.first of: the first of a word is its opening letter, here S
indicatorNotes.on: in an across answer, what comes on something is tacked on after it, so S follows TOTTER

blocks.note: one who tots up figures would be a totter

annotation.surface: Someone counting the steps of Scottish reels at a dance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reels' sounds like Scottish dances; it is the verb, to stagger. 'Presumably' admits TOTTER is an invented word for one who tots.
annotation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk unsteadily, so totters means reels.

entries.clue: Mysterious objects in lush heather, buried by earth (9)

indicatorNotes.buried by: in a down answer, what is buried lies beneath, so E sits on top

blocks.note: a lush is a drunk, as is a sot
Erica is the botanical name for heather

annotation.surface: Strange objects found in dense heather, covered over with soil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lush' looks like an adjective for thick heather; it is the noun, a drunkard.
annotation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure or mysterious items understood by few.

entries.clue: Cultivate ebony as cash crop (3,4)

indicatorNotes.Cultivate: to cultivate is to work over, reshaping the letters

annotation.surface: Advice to grow ebony trees as a profitable plantation crop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a link word but its letters are needed in the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: The soybean is grown widely as a commercial cash crop.

entries.clue: Recently delivered gas put away (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is adjectival, describing the newborn a neonate is

blocks.note: to put food away is to eat it

annotation.surface: A gas cylinder that has just been delivered is stored.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' reads as a parcel arriving; it is a baby being born.
annotation.definitionFit: From Greek and Latin 'newly born': a medical term for a baby in its first weeks after delivery.

entries.clue: Soldiers run away from restraints (7)

indicatorNotes.away from: to run away from something is to leave it, so R leaves LEGIRONS

blocks.note: R = run, from cricket scoring; it is removed

annotation.surface: Captive soldiers break free of their shackles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run away' reads as escaping; it splits into R and the removal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Legions are large bodies of soldiers, as in the Roman army.

entries.clue: Greatest resistance, say, put up in final (7)

indicatorNotes.put up: in a down answer, putting up reads the letters upwards, reversed
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places R and the upturned EG inside LAST, as a guest is put up in a house

annotation.surface: The strongest opposition is mounted in the final.
annotation.walkthrough: The sports-final picture hides that final is simply LAST, which opens to take in R and the upturned EG.
annotation.definitionFit: Largest means biggest, the greatest in size.

entries.clue: State makes vessels to deliver tea? (4)

indicatorNotes.State: to state is to say out loud

annotation.surface: A question about whether a state produces the vessels for serving tea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' pretends to be a country; it is the instruction to say the next word. EARNS and URNS sound alike in a British accent.
annotation.definitionFit: Tea urns are large vessels for serving tea; the question mark flags the definition by description.

entries.clue: Dinners for non-Ximenean cruciverbalist geeks? (5)

blocks.note: split the word as D IN NERS: the container is NERS, a non-word
first letter of the word, the D that goes in

annotation.surface: A question about what meals a rule-breaking crossword fan might eat.
annotation.walkthrough: Ximenes was a setter whose rules require every piece of wordplay to be a real word; the joke is that DINNERS, read as 'D in NERS', is a clue for NERDS only a rule-breaking solver would accept.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword enthusiasts, like other devotees of an obscure hobby, are cheerfully called nerds.

entries.clue: Competition solicitor adopting unbalanced manner (10)

indicatorNotes.adopting: to adopt is to take in, so TOUT holds the rest
indicatorNotes.unbalanced: letters thrown off balance are rearranged

annotation.surface: A lawyer entering a contest behaves erratically.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer; it is someone who solicits, a tout.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tournament is a sporting or games competition played in rounds.

entries.clue: Exercises by military vehicles essentially changing direction (5)

indicatorNotes.essentially changing direction: the essential, central letter, N for north, becomes another direction, S for south

annotation.surface: Army drills carried out by armoured vehicles that keep switching course.
annotation.walkthrough: Compass points N and S are both directions, so swapping one for the other changes direction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the school sense: exercises set for pupils are tasks to complete.

entries.clue: Désirée possibly, something used principally for mashing? (4)

annotation.definition: Désirée possibly, something used principally for mashing?

indicatorNotes.principally: principal means first, so only the first letters of the preceding words are used
indicatorNotes.mashing: mashed things are pulped out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first letters of Désirée, possibly, something, used

annotation.surface: A woman named Désirée, perhaps, and something mainly used for mashing.
annotation.walkthrough: Désirée is a popular red-skinned potato variety, not a woman. Read straight, the whole clue describes a potato; as wordplay, the heads of four words are mashed.
annotation.definitionFit: Spud is informal for potato, and Désirée is a potato variety.

entries.clue: Rock opera track one might take off (9)

indicatorNotes.Rock: to rock something is to shake it, disturbing the letters

annotation.surface: A song from a rock opera that someone might strip away or imitate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rock opera' is a single genre on the surface, like Tommy; split it and rock shakes up OPERA. 'Take off' then reads as copying rather than flight.
annotation.definitionFit: An aeroplane is the thing that takes off from a runway.

entries.clue: I struggle with suspicion of social climbers (5)

indicatorNotes.suspicion of: a suspicion is a mere trace, so only the first letter

annotation.surface: Someone confesses to mistrusting people trying to climb the social ladder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Social climbers' is a set phrase, but social is only providing its S; the climbers are plants.
annotation.definitionFit: By type: ivy is a climbing plant, and the plural covers several such climbers.

entries.clue: Spending last month dead relaxed (5)

indicatorNotes.Spending: what is spent is gone, so DEC is removed

blocks.note: Dec is December, the last month; it is removed

annotation.surface: Someone who spent the last month idle was dead to the world and relaxed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dead relaxed' reads as the slang for very relaxed, but dead gives DECEASED and relaxed stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to ease tension or a grip is to relax it.

entries.clue: Marry off sensationally lively Europeans (9)

indicatorNotes.off: when something comes off it is removed, so ALLY is taken away
indicatorNotes.lively: lively letters jump about into a new order

blocks.note: to ally is to join, as in marriage; it is removed

annotation.surface: A call to wed some wonderfully energetic Europeans.
annotation.walkthrough: SENSATIONALLY loses ALLY to leave SENSATION, which is shuffled.
annotation.definitionFit: Estonians are the people of Estonia in north-east Europe.
